title: Claim
description:
The Factory's unit of knowledge. Claims are append-only: a claim is never edited, it is superseded. This is what stops a hypothesis being quietly rewritten into a fact three weeks later — the single most important integrity rule in the system.

This file lives in shared/ but is also a stored artifact in its own right, because a claim is both a primitive embedded in other artifacts and a record on disk. Defining it twice would be the drift this structure exists to prevent.

tier.description: observed = measured or reported from a named source. derived = reasoned from other claims. hypothesis = asserted without evidence; legitimate, but must never be presented as fact.

source_uri.description: Where this came from. A URL, a portal page, a dataset id, or a playtest session id.

excerpt.description: The specific text or figure relied upon. Required in practice for review; keep it short and verbatim.

metric.description: Present when the evidence is quantitative.

method.description: How the source was read: web-fetch, played, listing, store-page, screenshot, video. A played observation also names its session.

session_id.description: The teardown session (game-record sessions[].id) this evidence comes from.

capture_uri.description: A recording, screenshot set or notes the excerpt can be checked against.

statement.description: One falsifiable sentence. 'Merge-2 idle games on Yandex average 6-9 minute sessions' — not 'merge is popular'.

parents.description: Claim ids this was reasoned from. Required for tier=derived.

support.description: The count a derived pattern or market statistic rests on. A share means nothing without its denominator, so a claim tagged `pattern` must carry one: how many members show it (numerator), out of how many were coded on the question at all (denominator), which do, and which do not.

members.description: Ids (games, titles) counted in the numerator.

exceptions.description: Ids in the denominator that do not show it.

unknown.description: Ids in scope but not coded on the counted facet: neither members nor exceptions, and not in the denominator.

frame.description: What was counted over: the corpus slice, list and date.

subject.description: What the claim is about, so claims can be retrieved by facet.

facet.description: Research-vocabulary facet the claim codes or counts.

superseded_by.description: Claim id that replaces this one. Set instead of editing. Once set, this claim is historical and must not be cited by new work.

then.description: An observed claim without a source is a hypothesis wearing a disguise.
A derived claim must say what it was derived from.
A hypothesis may not claim high confidence. If you are more sure than this, find evidence and restate it as observed or derived.
A pattern is derived from observations, and states its numerator and denominator.
Only a derived claim counts: an observation is one fact, and a hypothesis counts nothing.
